title: The contribution of school heterogeneity to subsequent wage inequality among young workers
title_hu: Az iskolák heterogenitásának hozzájárulása a későbbi béregyenlőtlenségekhez a fiatal munkavállalók esetében
summary_en: Does between-school variance in primary-and-secondary education translate into between-individual wage variance among young Hungarian workers? Horn and Boza link OKM school-test data with administrative wage records and decompose subsequent young-worker wage variance into a component explained by school attended vs. components explained by individual characteristics. They find that school-attended explains a non-trivial share of early-career wage variation, larger than in many OECD comparators.
policy_relevance: Direct relevance for Hungarian education-equity policy (BM Köznevelési Stratégia, NGM labour-market division) and for tracking the labour-market consequences of school-system inequalities. Supports the case that Hungarian school-segregation interventions deliver measurable downstream wage-inequality reductions, not just test-score-equity gains.
